note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right middle finger pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
41-year-old female presents with 4-5 days of pain at the tip of her right middle finger. Patient reports she was rear-ended in a motor vehicle accident at a four-way stop while stationary. The driver behind her appeared to be texting and did not notice she was stopped. Patient became angry and made a gesture toward the other driver, striking her right middle finger against the ceiling of her car with significant force. Minimal damage to vehicle (trunk crumpled). No other injuries sustained in the accident. Pain has persisted since the incident.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies pain in other areas. Otherwise unremarkable.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Atrial fibrillation.

MEDICATIONS
Digoxin.

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Involved in motor vehicle accident as driver while stopped at four-way stop. No other details provided.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Alert and oriented. Right hand examined. Tenderness appreciated over distal phalanx of right middle finger with palpation. No tenderness noted more distally. Otherwise normal examination.

RESULTS
X-ray of right hand shows distal phalanx fracture of the middle finger.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Distal phalanx fracture, right middle finger. Patient counseled that tramadol is safe to take concurrently with her digoxin for atrial fibrillation. Plan: (1) Tramadol 50 mg every 6 hours as needed for pain, 8 tablets dispensed for 2 days supply; (2) Finger splint applied; (3) Follow-up x-ray in 2 weeks to assess fracture healing. Patient instructed to return for follow-up appointment in 2 weeks.
